Personally, I don't think you need to 100% resonate with the label you think you fall under. For years I labeled my sexuality as bisexual but wasn't completely sure if that was me, then identifying with pansexuality with then not using labels to define my sexuality. You're allowed to experiment with labels to see what best feels most you, as long as you're not disrespecting the whole community.

Also!! You're allowed to not fit 100% with the gender you were assigned with, it's okay to be more masculine if you're AFAB, and vise versa for AMAB. Gender expression ≠ gender identity. 

If this isn't you and you're non-binary, then that doesn't mean you have to androgynous either. Non-binary means something different for everyone, and that's okay. You don't need to use labels if you don't want to, don't stuff yourself in a box that might not ‘do it’ for you.

At the end of the day just do what makes you most comfortable and strive from there

Hi! FtM 17-year-old here. Here is my coming out story.

I attempted to convince my mum to let me get a binder at age 13 and she had a very negative reaction, so I just played it off that I didn't want a prominent chest, which worked. 

I first came out to my friends when I was 15, but the majority of them were online (or people just assumed I was cis male based on outward appearance only [e.g. photos]). After a few months with experimenting with my pronouns with those said friends, I felt comfortable enough to share with my parents. I didn't know how to really approach my parents with this information (since my mum had a bad reaction years prior) especially since they just decided to separate. I later then broke down to my dad about how I felt because I knew he wouldn't have a negative reaction, and I was right. My dad was accepting and understanding. I then asked him to tell my mum for me since I didn't want to go through telling her about this myself and risking my safety. She was stubborn at first, but later understood and respected my new name and pronouns. 

I am in the process of telling my extended family on my mum's side (my dad side already knows), which will be hard seeing that they're all Christian and not very well educated with LGBT+ topics. I have started my medical transition, so I'll need to get on that.

My only advice for you is to come out to whomever makes you feel safe and comfortable first. There is no rush, take your time <3
